basis: Per 100 g of raw banana. A medium banana is about 118 g, so multiply by 1.2.

prebiotic_explainer.what: A prebiotic is a substrate that the microbes living in you use selectively, with a health benefit for you [14].
prebiotic_explainer.how: Resistant starch and pectin pass through the small intestine undigested. Gut bacteria in the colon ferment them into short-chain fatty acids, including butyrate, the main fuel for the cells lining your colon [15][6].
prebiotic_explainer.why: A banana's prebiotic content is not fixed: ripening converts the resistant starch into sugar, so the greener the banana, the more prebiotic it carries [2][3].

unripe.headline_label: resistant starch and other fibre per 100 g
unripe.summary: A green banana is the prebiotic peak. Measured with the method that captures resistant starch, an unripe banana holds about 18 g of fibre per 100 g — roughly 64% of the 28 g daily fibre value, and about four times what a ripe one has [2][16].
unripe.gut: That resistant starch and the pectin alongside it reach the colon intact, where gut bacteria ferment them into short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate [6][15]. If you are eating bananas for your gut, this is the stage to pick.

facts.label: Fructans (FODMAP)
facts.note: firm unripe bananas are low-FODMAP up to about 100 g

ripe.headline_label: resistant starch and other fibre per 100 g
ripe.summary: By the time a banana is yellow, most of the resistant starch has become sugar. Fibre measured the same way falls to about 4-5 g per 100 g, around 16% of the daily fibre value, while sugars climb to roughly 15 g [2][16].
ripe.gut: There is still some resistant starch and pectin for your gut bacteria to ferment [6][15], just a fraction of what a green banana offers. A firmer, just-yellow banana keeps more of it than a spotted one [2].

facts.label: Fructans (FODMAP)
facts.note: tolerance drops once brown spots appear

overripe.headline_label: resistant starch and other fibre per 100 g
overripe.summary: A heavily spotted banana has nearly finished converting starch to sugar. Fibre measured with the resistant-starch method drops to about 2 g per 100 g — roughly 7% of the daily fibre value, and about a ninth of a green banana's [2][16].
overripe.gut: Very little resistant starch is left to feed your gut bacteria [2][3]. The sweetness and the antioxidants peak here, but for prebiotics this is the weakest stage.

facts.label: Fructans (FODMAP)
facts.note: keep to a small serving if fructan-sensitive

rotten.summary: Spoiled fruit is not a prebiotic question. Mouldy soft fruit should be thrown out whole, because the mould roots below the surface [9].
rotten.gut: Whatever fibre remains is not worth the risk of mould toxins [8][9]. Compost it and scan a fresher banana.

baseline.title: Every banana, any stage
baseline.note: USDA publishes one entry for raw banana regardless of ripeness, so these hold roughly steady as it ripens [1][2].

rows.label: Carbohydrate
rows.note: the starch-to-sugar split shifts with ripeness
